transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello, doctor. Well, I suppose what brings me in is this memorial I'm putting together for my brother. It’s... well, it's gotten a lot bigger than I originally meant it to. 

I’ve been spending most of my days lately chasing down songs, calling folks up, and planning out all these displays and trips for it. My wife is the one who pushed me to come see you. She says I’ve completely pushed aside the garden, my walking group, and just about everything else I normally do.
When did your brother pass away?
About two months ago. That's... well, that's when all this really started. It's been going on for about two months now, ever since he passed and I began putting this tribute together for him.

When you're working on this memorial project, do you feel like you can stop yourself from thinking about it and working on it, or does it feel like something you have to keep doing even when you want to take a break?

I really can't stop. I mean, even if I tell myself to take a break, I just can’t seem to sit in my chair like I used to. I just have to keep moving. I’m constantly up hauling boxes around, making phone calls, rearranging all these papers for the displays... or just walking from room to room. 

It feels like my body has more steam in it than a man my age ought to have, to be honest. So, no, sitting down and resting just isn't really happening right now.
Besides the energy and the constant movement, how would you describe your overall mood right now? Do you feel unusually good, excited, or optimistic about things in general?

Well, it's... it's a mix, I suppose. I do feel unusually good a lot of the time. I'll feel just lit up and full of purpose, like I'm doing something really important. I get this feeling that the whole town is finally going to understand our family and what my brother meant. But then... well, it flips. If my wife tries to slow me down, or if someone down at the senior center questions how I'm setting up a display, I just snap at them. I get real short-tempered if anyone gets in the way of what I'm trying to do.

When you say you feel 'lit up and full of purpose,' would you say your mood feels abnormally high or elevated compared to how you normally feel—like you're on top of the world in a way that's unusual for you—or does it feel more like normal happiness tied to doing something meaningful?

Well, it definitely feels higher than normal. I mean, I'm usually a pretty quiet guy, but right now... yeah, it's like I'm on top of the world. I feel like this project is the most important thing I've ever done, and I just get so fired up about it. Like I said before, I'll be feeling great, thinking about how everyone is going to see what my brother meant to this town... but it doesn't always stay that way. If someone interrupts me, or my wife tells me I need to sit down and rest, that high feeling turns right into anger. I just get so irritated if anyone tries to get in my way. So it's not just normal happiness, it's... it's a lot more intense, and it can turn into me snapping at people pretty quick.

Before your brother passed away two months ago, have you ever had periods—lasting days or weeks—where you felt this same kind of elevated, fired-up mood with lots of energy and racing thoughts, even when nothing particular was happening in your life?

No, I can't say that I have. I've always just been a pretty steady, quiet kind of guy. I mean, I've had good days and bad days like anyone else, but nothing like this. This... this fired-up feeling and having all this energy, it's really just been since I started working on the memorial project for my brother. Before he passed, I never had anything like this happen.
